exposure: Health system factors (prolonged abnormal observations without action, delay in starting treatment, lack of blood transfusion)
cohort: The study cohort comprises women who experienced maternal death across all district and central hospitals in Malawi between 2020 and 2022, along with facility-level aggregated birth data.
finding: Despite a low national CS rate, over half of maternal deaths occurred following CS, with women delivering by CS being five times more likely to die than those delivering vaginally.
mod_finding: Women who delivered by CS were five times more likely to die than women who delivered vaginally, and deaths from pregnancy-related infection were more often associated with CS.
